text:
Maria Chen: Quick sync — I'm drafting a spec for tenant-level burst capacity + customer-managed networking costs. Need product/eng/ops take. High-level options are 1) soft quota with auto-throttle + per-tenant IP pooling, or 2) strict quota + per-tenant reserved bursts (paid).
Arjun Patel: do we have customer asks that force option 2?
Maria Chen: A few enterprise customers asked for guaranteed burst windows for batch workloads (end-of-month scoring). They want stable egress IPs + guaranteed slots.
Sara Lopez: for VPC customers, static egress IP + reserved slots makes sense. But it complicates upgrades and rollback windows.
Devon Brooks: versioning concern — reserved bursts tie capacity to a specific runtime build unless we decouple with a handshake token. That adds infra work.
Maria Chen: noted. I'm sketching rollout constraints: canary group (10% tenants), upgrade window 2 hours, fallback to shared pool if handshake fails. Need metric thresholds for canary success. Suggestions?
Arjun Patel: key metrics: 95th latency, token/sec per tenant, and % requests routed to shared pool during canary. Also error-rate delta vs baseline.
Sara Lopez: add SLO for DNS resolution time for customer-managed IPs — we've seen weird timeouts in onprem installs.
Maria Chen: good call. Also pricing impact: reserved bursts mean we reserve GPUs for N hours — cost model needs to show amortized per-tenant hourly rate.
Devon Brooks: sample config for the handshake I'm proposing: 
```yaml
burst_policy:
  mode: reserved  # reserved | shared
  reserved_hours: 2
  ip_pool: tenant-static
  handshake_timeout_s: 45
  fallback: shared_pool
```
Devon Brooks: handshake_timeout_s 45 should cover slow onprem controllers. If handshake fails we fallback immediately to avoid impacting latency.
Maria Chen: ops question — who owns the rollback policy if canary fails? product or eng-oncall?
Sara Lopez: product defines the threshold, eng-oncall flips the rollout, ops owns comms.
Maria Chen: noted. Action items: @Arjun to draft metric dashboard for canary (due EOD Tue), @Devon to prototype handshake with fallback (PR by Fri), @Sara to scope DNS/TCP flaky cases and mitigation steps (sync Wed). I'll update the roadmap doc after that and include pricing mockups. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: Deployment pipeline report: canary-env image built (sha: df3a9b), tests passed. https://ci.internal/reports/df3a9b
Arjun Patel: sounds good. one more ask — include an explicit network ops checklist for customers who want to reserve IPs (ipam, peering, CIDR collisions). That reduces support tickets.
Maria Chen: agree. I'll add a 'field-install checklist' section. Thanks all — will ping when the draft is in the roadmap doc (link to follow).
